aiOverview.content: The World Health Organization (WHO) is a specialized United Nations agency responsible for international public health, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. Founded to promote health, keep the world safe, and serve the vulnerable, it coordinates responses to health emergencies, sets global standards, and monitors health trends. Key aspects of the WHO include: Mission: To promote health, keep the world safe, and serve the vulnerable, with a goal of achieving the highest possible level of health for all people. Leadership: It leads global efforts on health emergencies, such as COVID-19, Zika, and Ebola, while tackling communicable and non-communicable diseases. Structure: It operates with 194 Member States, 6 regional offices, and 150+ field offices, staffed by experts. Goals (Triple Billion Targets): Aims to have 1 billion more people benefiting from universal health coverage, 1 billion more better protected from health emergencies, and 1 billion more enjoying better health and well-being. Functions: Sets health norms and standards, develops evidence-based policies, monitors health trends (e.g., mortality data), and provides technical support to countries. The WHO is dedicated to a healthier, safer world, guided by science to provide everyone, everywhere an equal chance at a healthy life.
